```plato
    //==
    // # Building a cloth — from a polygon mesh
    //
    // The same graph derived from an arbitrary `PolygonMesh3D`: one vertex per
    // position, one structural spring per undirected edge, and one dihedral
    // bend constraint per interior edge. Rest lengths and rest angles come from
    // the mesh's own geometry, so the cloth starts exactly at rest whatever
    // shape it was authored in.
    //
    // Cost: `PolygonMesh3D` answers incidence queries by scanning its packed
    // corner table rather than from a stored adjacency structure
    // (`meshes-polygon.library.plato` states the complexity), so this build is
    // cubic in corner count. It is a build step, run once, not part of a step.

    // One cloth vertex per mesh position, at rest and free.
    MeshClothVertices(self: PolygonMesh3D, vertexMass: Mass): Array<ClothVertex>
        => self.Positions.Map(p => ClothVertex(p, p, SafeDivide(1.0, vertexMass.Kilograms, 0.0), false));

    // The structural spring for one undirected edge, at its current length.
    MeshSpring(self: PolygonMesh3D, edge: UndirectedEdgeIndex, compliance: Number): ClothDistanceConstraint
    {
        var ends = self.VerticesOfUndirectedEdge(edge);
        return ClothDistanceConstraint(ends.A, ends.B,
            new Length(self.Positions[ends.A.Value].Distance(self.Positions[ends.B.Value])),
            compliance);
    }

    // One structural spring per undirected edge of the mesh.
    MeshSprings(self: PolygonMesh3D, compliance: Number): Array<ClothDistanceConstraint>
        => self.UndirectedEdgeCount.MapRange(e => self.MeshSpring(UndirectedEdgeIndex(e), compliance));

    // The first vertex of a face that is neither end of an edge: the wing a
    // dihedral bend constraint folds about. Returns the "none" index when the
    // face has no such vertex.
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Typed indices - -1 means none.
    WingVertex(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: FaceIndex, ends: VertexPair): VertexIndex
        => self.VerticesOfFace(face).Reduce(VertexIndex(-1), (found, v) =>
            found.IsNone.And(v.Equals(ends.A).Not).And(v.Equals(ends.B).Not) ? v : found);

    // True when an undirected edge is shared by two faces, which is what a
    // dihedral bend constraint needs. A boundary edge has one.
    IsInteriorEdge(self: PolygonMesh3D, edge: UndirectedEdgeIndex): Boolean
        => self.FacesOfUndirectedEdge(edge).Count >= 2;

    // The bend constraint across one interior edge, its rest angle the angle
    // the mesh already has there. Precondition: the edge is interior and both
    // its faces have a vertex off the edge.
    MeshBendConstraint(self: PolygonMesh3D, edge: UndirectedEdgeIndex, compliance: Number): ClothBendConstraint
    {
        var ends = self.VerticesOfUndirectedEdge(edge);
        var faces = self.FacesOfUndirectedEdge(edge);
        var wingC = self.WingVertex(faces[0], ends);
        var wingD = self.WingVertex(faces[1], ends);
        return ClothBendConstraint(ends.A, ends.B, wingC, wingD,
            DihedralAngle(self.Positions[ends.A.Value], self.Positions[ends.B.Value],
                          self.Positions[wingC.Value], self.Positions[wingD.Value]),
            compliance);
    }

    // One bend constraint per interior edge. Boundary edges are folded out
    // rather than emitted with a "none" wing, so every constraint the solver
    // sees names four real vertices.
    MeshBendConstraints(self: PolygonMesh3D, compliance: Number): Array<ClothBendConstraint>
        => self.UndirectedEdgeCount.MapRange(e => UndirectedEdgeIndex(e))
            .Reduce(ClothBendConstraint.NoBendConstraints, (kept, e) =>
                self.IsInteriorEdge(e) ? kept.Append(self.MeshBendConstraint(e, compliance)) : kept);

    // A cloth over any polygon mesh, with the mesh's own face table kept so the
    // result reads back out as the same mesh. Vertex numbering is the mesh's:
    // cloth vertex i is mesh position i.
    ClothFromMesh(self: PolygonMesh3D, vertexMass: Mass, compliance: Number, thickness: Length): ClothMesh3D
        => ClothMesh3D(
            Cloth3D(
                self.MeshClothVertices(vertexMass),
                self.MeshSprings(compliance),
                self.MeshBendConstraints(compliance),
                self.ToTriangleMesh.Faces,
                thickness),
            self.Faces);

    //==
    // # The position-based solver
    //
    // Predict, then project. Each substep integrates every vertex forward under
    // the external forces alone, then sweeps the constraints until the
    // predicted positions satisfy them; the velocity for the next substep falls
    // out of the corrected positions with no separate update, because that is
    // what Verlet state means.
    //
    // This is the solver that is stable at any stiffness, which is why it is
    // the one people ship: the projection can only ever move a vertex TOWARD
    // satisfying a constraint, so no amount of stiffness can add energy.
    //
    // Contacts are not applied here. Compose them after a step —
    // `cloth.Step(...).CollideWith(sphere).CollideWith(ground)` — which is the
    // right order: the solve settles the cloth, then the contact has the last
    // word on where a vertex is allowed to be.

    // One substep of position-based dynamics over a cloth.
    SubStep(self: Cloth3D, forces: ParticleForces3D, settings: ClothSolverSettings, time: Number, dt: Duration): Cloth3D
    {
        var stiffness = IterationStiffness(settings.Stiffness, settings.IterationCount);
        var predicted = self.Vertices.Map(v =>
            v.Integrate(forces.AccelerationAt(v.Position, v.Velocity(dt), time), dt, settings.VelocityDamping));
        var stretched = SolveDistance(predicted, self.DistanceConstraints, settings.IterationCount, stiffness, dt);
        return self.WithVertices(
            SolveBend(stretched, self.BendConstraints, settings.IterationCount, stiffness));
    }

    // One whole step: `SubStepCount` substeps of `TimeStep / SubStepCount`
    // each. Substepping is the cheapest accuracy there is here — n substeps of
    // one iteration converge better than one substep of n iterations, because
    // each substep also re-reads the forces.
    Step(self: Cloth3D, forces: ParticleForces3D, settings: ClothSolverSettings, time: Number): Cloth3D
    {
        var seconds = SafeDivide(settings.TimeStep.Seconds, settings.SubStepCount.ToNumber, settings.TimeStep.Seconds);
        return settings.SubStepCount.MapRange(i => i)
            .Reduce(self, (current, i) =>
                current.SubStep(forces, settings, time + i.ToNumber * seconds, new Duration(seconds)));
    }

    // One whole step of a mesh-bound cloth; the face table is carried through
    // untouched.
    Step(self: ClothMesh3D, forces: ParticleForces3D, settings: ClothSolverSettings, time: Number): ClothMesh3D
        => ClothMesh3D(self.Cloth.Step(forces, settings, time), self.Faces);
```
